newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to go on holiday July 7, venue undecided.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to go on holiday July 7, venue undecided.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will begin a holiday on July 7, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing on Monday.

The president, who he said last week would definitely take time off in Russia, would decide exactly where he was going by the end of this week and would also announce then how long he would be gone from Moscow.
Yastrzhembsky said last week Yeltsin would not go to his once favourite Black Sea resort of Sochi, where he cut short a holiday in May complaining of bad weather.
At least two regional leaders, including the head of the Karelia region on the Finnish border, had urged the president to take his break in their areas, he said.

Yeltsin, 66, caused some renewed concern about his health when he missed an engagement at the Group of Seven summit in Denver on June 21 but looked cheerful and well towards the end of his time there.
He appeared in Moscow last Friday and has a full programme of work and meetings this week, the spokesman said.

He will meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his two first deputies, Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, on Tuesday along with the head of Yeltsin's presidential administration Valentin Yumashev.

They will discuss events over the first half of the year and how to better coordinate the work of the government and the presidential staff. Yastrzhembsky said meetings of this group would become routine from now on.
Yeltsin will record his weekly radio address on Wednesday for broadcast on Friday and host talks and a state reception for visiting Azeri President Haydar Aliyev on Thursday.
On Friday, he will meet regional administration chiefs.
